title: Radians, Arc Length and Sector Area
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Maths: Radians Worksheets
standard_text: Work with radian measure, including use for arc length and area of a sector; understand and use the standard small angle approximations.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level maths worksheets on radians: converting degrees and radians, arc length rθ, sector area ½r²θ, segments and perimeters. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Arc length = rθ; sector area = ½r²θ (θ in radians).
body_html:
How it works

π radians = 180°, so 1 radian ≈ 57.3°. With θ in radians: arc length s = rθ and sector area A = ½r²θ. Segment area = ½r²(θ − sin θ).

Example

Arc length, r = 6 cm, θ = π/3.

6 × π/3

Answer: 2π cm

Common mistakes

  • Using degrees in rθ.
  • Forgetting the two radii in a sector's perimeter.
  • Setting the calculator to degrees for sin θ in the segment formula.

faq.q: How do you convert degrees to radians?
faq.a: Multiply by π/180. For example, 90° = π/2 radians.

faq.q: What is the area of a sector in radians?
faq.a: ½r²θ, where θ is the angle at the centre in radians.

items.q: A round cake of radius 18 cm is cut into 6 equal sectors. Find the area of the top of one piece, correct to 3 significant figures.
